messages:
maria_p: kicking off a short PRD intake thread for the 'alpha gates' launch criteria. problem statement: several enterprise beta customers want safer model updates — automatic quick rollbacks when a new model variant causes a measurable drop in task-level quality for that customer's traffic. we need a lightweight, low-friction gate that can operate per-route and per-customer without adding major infra complexity. :wave:

maria_p: goals: 1) define clear success/failure metrics for gated rollouts, 2) specify required signals and tolerances (accuracy/regressions, latency P95), 3) list non-goals (not building a full canary platform or redoing long-term eval infra), 4) propose minimal acceptance criteria for GA.

kevin_eng: quick q — should this live as a routing policy in the control plane (preferred) or do we need per-GW feature flags? trying to scope infra work.

henry_ml: +1 to control-plane policy. for metrics, propose: 
```
- quality_signal: task_accuracy (per-customer, rolling 1h)
- regression_trigger: drop >= 2.5% absolute AND 3-sigma vs baseline
- latency_trigger: 95th > baseline_95th * 1.35 for >15m
- sample_size_min: 500 requests in the window
```
These are starting numbers; we should validate with customer traffic profiles. :mag: 

samira_csm: from customers i've talked to — they care most about per-customer accuracy and false-positive rate. some will accept a slightly higher latency during alpha but will not tolerate content regressions. also they want a clear rollback window and a way to opt out for specific endpoints.

ida_design: one UX ask: how will we surface the gate state in Console? small idea: per-route banner + historical small sparkline and a 'why blocked' tooltip linking to the metric that fired. keeps it lightweight.

kevin_eng: infra constraints: we can implement a control-plane guard that evaluates aggregated signals from our observability pipeline (metrics store). two implementation options: 
1) synchronous quick-check: each rollout update hits the gate which queries recent metrics (fast, but adds coupling)
2) async evaluation + auto-rollback: rollout proceeds, but a watchdog monitors and can trigger rollback within a window. option 2 is safer for rollout speed but needs reliable rollback automation.

maria_p: non-goals (for alpha): 1) no multi-variant A/B analysis platform, 2) no per-customer custom model variants, 3) no long-term drift remediation automation. keep alpha focused on detection + automated rollback and a manual override.

henry_ml: acceptance criteria (alpha): 
- gate evaluates per-route and per-customer for 95% of customer traffic patterns (not edge-case tiny customers)
- metrics computed with sample_size_min and triggers (see snippet)
- rollback completes within 90s of trigger detection 90% of the time
- audit log entry + reason visible in Console and in account activity logs
- integration tests covering simulated regression and latency spikes

samira_csm: success metrics we can present to customers: 
- % of rollouts that auto-rollback due to quality triggers (goal: <5% false positive)
- mean time to rollback when triggered (goal: <2 minutes)
- customer opt-outs used (monitor usage)
- customer satisfaction in post-alpha interviews (qualitative)

ida_design: small sketch idea for alert copy: 
"Alpha Gate: model rollout paused — accuracy dropped 3.1% vs baseline (window: 1h). click for details and rollback history."

kevin_eng: edge cases to call out: 
- cold-start traffic patterns where baseline is poorly estimated for small customers
- flakey telemetry (missing metrics) — gate should be conservative and prefer manual hold if metrics are insufficient
- model variant changes that shift distribution (e.g., generation length) which may change token-level latency but not task quality

maria_p: proposed next steps: 
1) agree on metric thresholds and sample size (action: henry_ml + kevin_eng) by EOD thursday
2) infra spike to validate async watchdog rollback feasibility (action: kevin_eng)
3) Console mockups for alpha indicators (action: ida_design)
4) draft alpha acceptance doc for legal/compliance review (action: maria_p)

kevin_eng: i can do the infra spike next sprint. for the rollback automation, we should simulate both short and long rollbacks.

henry_ml: i'll run synthetic evals against a few internal test models and a small customer dataset to tune the 2.5%/3-sigma initial numbers.

samira_csm: i'll compile the customer ask examples and opt-out scenarios to include in the PRD.

maria_p: thanks all. can people react with :thumbsup: if they agree with the plan or leave short objections. planning to open a ticket once we have the thresholds.

qa-bot: test-plan template created: https://redwood.internal/tests/alpha-gates-template

jira-bot: created ticket INF-4124: "alpha rollout gates — alpha acceptance + watchdog" and linked to this thread.

kevin_eng: :+1:
